Veronica Fernandez

End The Corruption! candidate for United States Senator, New Jersey · Challenger

Small business owner (co-owns a commercial electrical contracting business); former licensed property casualty insurance underwriter

Veronica Fernandez, 67, grew up in Franklin, New Jersey, and lives in Long Valley, Morris County. She worked for 20 years as a property casualty insurance underwriter and has run a small business since 2006. She is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for U.S. Senate under the "End the Corruption!" designation, after qualifying by petition with 2,451 signatures.

Where Fernandez stands

Health care
Supports Medicare for All. Says insurance is meant to cover loss, not ongoing care, and calls health insurance companies "entirely unnecessary middlemen."
Campaign finance
Supports campaign finance reform and efforts to overturn the 2010 Citizens United v. FEC decision. Says the country needs "fundamental structural change."
Economy and cost of living
Says steps must be taken to make life more affordable for New Jerseyans, pointing to gas and grocery prices, and argues the economy needs "a working-class Congress."
Israel and Gaza
Says she would vote against sending money to Israel. Calls Prime Minister Netanyahu a war criminal and describes Israel's actions in Gaza as genocide.
Iran war
Opposes the war in Iran. Says it was unnecessary and unaffordable, and argues President Trump is adding to the deficit.
